geo.label: 2026 Iran war began on 28 February 2026
geo.text: The United States and Israel began strikes on Iran on 28 February 2026 (Operation Epic Fury, US; Roaring Lion, Israel). Ali Khamenei was killed in the first strikes. Iran retaliated against Israel, US bases and Gulf states, and closed the Strait of Hormuz to most shipping.
geo.source: House of Commons Library (2026); Wikipedia (2026 Iran war)

geo.label: Iran ceasefire and MoU collapsed; fighting resumed 8 July 2026
geo.text: A two-week ceasefire mediated by Pakistan was agreed on 7 April 2026. A June 2026 memorandum collapsed; the US and Iran resumed fighting on 8 July; the MoU formally expired in August. As of September 2026 the two were again trading limited strikes (CRS R48887).
geo.source: CRS (R48887, Sep 2026); Wikipedia (2026 Iran war ceasefire)

geo.label: Israel-Lebanon ceasefires (16 April and 1-4 June 2026)
geo.text: Israel and Lebanon agreed a ceasefire effective 16 April 2026. Israel and Hezbollah agreed a truce on 1 June 2026, and a conditional Israel-Lebanon ceasefire was announced on 4 June 2026. Hezbollah has not accepted every term, and fighting continued in the south (Al Jazeera; AP).
geo.source: Al Jazeera (4 Jun 2026); AP (2 Jun 2026); Wikipedia (2026 Israel-Lebanon ceasefire)

geo.label: Gaza ceasefire since 10 October 2025; Israel holds more than 63% of the Strip
geo.text: The ceasefire under the US-backed plan took effect on 10 October 2025. Israel has expanded the area inside the Yellow Line and holds more than 63% of the Gaza Strip, per Gaza's Health Ministry and government media office. More than 1,478 Palestinians were reported killed since the ceasefire took effect.

scs.label: Strait of Hormuz: crude shipments down 95%, LNG down 99%
scs.text: WTO data cited by the House of Commons Library show a 95 per cent reduction in ships carrying crude oil to and from Persian Gulf ports and a 99 per cent reduction in ships carrying LNG since the conflict began. The UAE's state oil company estimates full flows will not resume until 2027.

milops.label: Iranian missiles hit US bases in Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and the UAE (28 February 2026)
milops.text: Iranian ballistic missiles and drones targeted Al Udeid (Qatar), Ali Al Salem (Kuwait), Al Dhafra (UAE) and the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain. Bahrain confirmed the Fifth Fleet headquarters was hit. These are reported targets and confirmations by the countries concerned.
milops.source: France 24 (28 Feb 2026); Middle East Eye (28 Feb 2026); Wikipedia (2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain)

milops.label: Pentagon inspector general: hundreds of buildings damaged at US bases in the region
milops.text: The Pentagon's inspector general reports that Iranian strikes damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman and Jordan during the conflict (CSMonitor).

milops.label: Iranian drones and missiles strike Oman's ports (2026)
milops.text: Iranian drone and missile strikes have targeted the ports of Duqm and Salalah, which the US uses, and the ports and industrial zones of Sohar, Bukha and Mina al Fahal, with attacks in Omani waters of the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf of Oman (Wikipedia, 2026 Iranian strikes on Oman).

milops.label: Houthis resume attacks on Israel (28 March 2026)
milops.text: The Houthis resumed their attacks on Israel on 28 March 2026, after pausing them following the 2025 Gaza ceasefire, and joined the Iran war with ballistic missiles. They have repeatedly threatened the Bab el-Mandeb strait (Wikipedia).

milops.label: Israeli strikes on Iran's missile and drone sites (2026)
milops.text: Critical Threats reports strikes on Iranian missile bases at Bid Ganeh (2 March 2026), Kashan (2 March), Esfahan South (3 March, the third strike there) and Dezful (4 March), and on drone launch sites in south-eastern Iran (1 March). These are satellite-imagery assessments by a US think tank.

naval.label: US strikes on Bandar Abbas naval base (28 February to 5 March 2026)
naval.text: The United States struck the Iranian naval base at Bandar Abbas on at least 28 February, 2 March and 5 March 2026. Satellite imagery shows the forward base ship IRIS Makran on fire at its pier. The IRIN's main naval headquarters was reported moved to Jask.
naval.source: FDD Long War Journal (Mar 2026); USNI News (2 Mar 2026)

naval.label: US unmanned boats strike Bandar Abbas submarine facility (12 July 2026)
naval.text: CENTCOM said three autonomous Saronic Corsair boats struck a raised dock at Bandar Abbas. A maritime analysis reports that the hoist used to lift submarines was destroyed, along with a Ghadir midget submarine in it.
naval.source: Interesting Engineering (14 Jul 2026, citing CENTCOM); Maritime News (14 Jul 2026)

naval.label: Israel's sixth submarine, INS Drakon, arrives at Haifa (September 2026)
naval.text: INS Drakon, the third Dolphin II boat and the sixth submarine in Israel's fleet, arrived at Haifa in late September 2026 after 23 days at sea from Germany. Israel's five existing Dolphin-class boats are based at Haifa; the Dakar class is planned from 2033.

naval.label: Turkey's Reis-class submarines: S-330 and S-331 in service
naval.text: Piri Reis (S-330) was commissioned on 24 August 2024 and Hızır Reis (S-331) on 27 November 2025. Both were built at Gölcük Naval Shipyard. Murat Reis (S-332) was launched in May 2025, and three more are under construction.

arms.label: Israeli and US strikes on Iran's nuclear sites (June 2025)
arms.text: Israel struck Natanz on 13 June 2025 and the Khondab (Arak) reactor on 19 June. The US struck Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan on 22 June 2025 (Operation Midnight Hammer). The ceasefire took effect on 24 June 2025. Damage assessments differ, and the IAEA's access to Iranian sites was limited after 13 June 2025.
arms.source: CRS (IF13032); Armscontrol.org (25 Jun 2025); Al Jazeera (19 Jun 2025)

arms.label: IAEA: projectiles struck near Bushehr nuclear plant (March and April 2026)
arms.text: The IAEA reported that a structure about 350 metres from the Bushehr reactor was hit and destroyed on 18 March 2026, and that a projectile struck close to the premises on 4 April 2026, the fourth such incident in recent weeks.
arms.source: ANS / Nuclear Newswire (6 Apr 2026, citing the IAEA)

arms.label: HESA drone plant in Shahin Shahr struck (1-2 March 2026)
arms.text: Satellite imagery shows at least nine impact points and five damaged buildings at HESA's Shahin Shahr facility, which produces Ababil and Shahed drones, from strikes on 1-2 March 2026 (Critical Threats).

arms.label: Masyaf underground missile plant destroyed by Israeli strikes (2024)
arms.text: Israeli strikes on the Masyaf site in Syria destroyed or damaged 140 targets and killed 230 people, including 208 fighters. The underground missile plant, reportedly Iran-linked, was described as one of several Iranian missile facilities built in Syria since 2018.

air.label: Kuwait International Airport struck by drones (March 2026)
air.text: Iranian drones struck Kuwait International Airport and a residential building, wounding two people (Stripes, 1 March 2026). Kuwait's air defences said they had mistakenly shot down three US aircraft the same day.

air.label: Russia-Syria MoU on Hmeimim and Tartus (9 August 2026)
air.text: Syria and Russia signed a memorandum on the future of the two bases after 18 months of talks. Military facilities become joint training and capacity-building centres; Syria takes over civilian sites, including Hmeimim airport and Tartus Pier No. 4, within three months. Russian personnel remain. Al Jazeera said Russia's presence had fallen from more than 100 military sites to these two.
air.source: Al Jazeera (9 Aug 2026); Moscow Times (9 Aug 2026); Kiprinform (11 Aug 2026)

econ.label: QatarEnergy halts LNG production after Iranian attacks (March 2026)
econ.text: QatarEnergy, one of the world's largest LNG producers, halted production after Iranian attacks on 2 March 2026 (Al Jazeera).

social.label: Civilians killed in Iranian attacks on Israel before the April 2026 ceasefire (reported)
social.text: The Congressional Research Service reports that 20 Israeli civilians were reportedly killed in Iranian attacks before the 7 April 2026 ceasefire. Iran says at least 610 of its citizens were killed in the June 2025 war (Al Jazeera).
social.source: CRS (R48887, Sep 2026); Al Jazeera (24 Jun 2025 timeline)

wellbeing.label: World Happiness Report 2026: country ranks not verified in this build for these 17 states
wellbeing.text: The annual report ranks countries for wellbeing. The ranks for these 17 states were not verified in this build; check the report directly.
wellbeing.source: World Happiness Report (annual); not verified in this build

markers.name: Manama (capital, Bahrain)
markers.note: Capital of Bahrain.

markers.name: Nicosia (capital, Cyprus)
markers.note: Capital of Cyprus; the island is divided, and the Turkish-Cypriot north is not drawn separately.

markers.name: Cairo (capital, Egypt)
markers.note: Capital of Egypt.

markers.name: Tehran (capital, Iran)
markers.note: Capital of Iran; the 2026 war has included strikes across the country.

markers.name: Baghdad (capital, Iraq)
markers.note: Capital of Iraq.

markers.name: Jerusalem (seat of government, Israel)
markers.note: Israel's seat of government. The status of Jerusalem is disputed; the map does not settle it.

markers.name: Amman (capital, Jordan)
markers.note: Capital of Jordan.

markers.name: Kuwait City (capital, Kuwait)
markers.note: Capital of Kuwait.

markers.name: Beirut (capital, Lebanon)
markers.note: Capital of Lebanon. Israel has said it will not strike Beirut's southern suburbs under the June 2026 arrangement (per Al Jazeera).

markers.name: Muscat (capital, Oman)
markers.note: Capital of Oman. Oman has been the venue for US-Iran talks in 2025 and 2026 (per Al Jazeera).

markers.name: Ramallah (seat of the Palestinian Authority)
markers.note: Seat of the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank. Palestine's status is contested.

markers.name: Doha (capital, Qatar)
markers.note: Capital of Qatar.

markers.name: Riyadh (capital, Saudi Arabia)
markers.note: Capital of Saudi Arabia; explosions were reported over Riyadh on 28 Feb 2026 (AFP, Al Jazeera).

markers.name: Damascus (capital, Syria)
markers.note: Capital of Syria.

markers.name: Ankara (capital, Turkey)
markers.note: Capital of Turkey; the Turkish Fleet Command's defence-industry partners ASELSAN, Roketsan and TAI are in or near Ankara.

markers.name: Sanaa (Houthi-controlled area; capital of Yemen)
markers.note: Sanaa is under Houthi control in the reporting used here. The internationally recognised government is based in Aden. Shown as reported, not as a judgement.

markers.name: Abu Dhabi (capital, UAE)
markers.note: Capital of the United Arab Emirates. A civilian was killed by debris from Iranian missile interceptions in Abu Dhabi on 28 Feb 2026 (France 24).

markers.name: Al Udeid Air Base (Qatar): largest US base in the region
markers.note: Forward-deployed HQ for US Air Force and Army assets. About 10,000 US troops (CSMonitor, 2026). Iranian ballistic missile hit it on 3-4 March 2026 (Wikipedia, 2026 in Qatar); Iran fired missiles at it on 23 June 2025.
markers.source: CSMonitor (29 Sep 2026); Wikipedia (2026 in Qatar; 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar); France 24

markers.name: Al Dhafra Air Base (UAE): US Air Force hub for advanced air warfare training
markers.note: US Air Force hub for advanced air warfare training; combat aircraft rotate through it (France 24). Smoke rose from the base after explosions in Abu Dhabi on 28 Feb 2026. Position approximate.

markers.name: Ali Al Salem Air Base (Kuwait): 386th Air Expeditionary Wing
markers.note: Primary airlift hub for US forces in the region (386th Air Expeditionary Wing, per the US military). Targeted by Iranian ballistic missiles on 28 Feb 2026 (Fars claim, reported by Middle East Eye and France 24). Position approximate.
markers.source: France 24 (28 Feb 2026); Middle East Eye (28 Feb 2026)

markers.name: Camp Arifjan (Kuwait): forward HQ of the US Army component of CENTCOM
markers.note: Forward headquarters for the US Army component of US Central Command (France 24). Position approximate.

markers.name: Camp Buehring (Kuwait): US Army camp
markers.note: Named among the US installations in Kuwait (CSMonitor, 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Prince Sultan Air Base (Saudi Arabia): US presence
markers.note: Named among the permanent or semi-permanent US bases in the region (CSMonitor, 2026). A 2026 analysis reports Shahed-drone waves against it; that is an analyst's account (Quwa), not a government statement. Position approximate.

markers.name: Naval Support Activity Bahrain: US Navy Fifth Fleet headquarters
markers.note: US Navy Fifth Fleet and US Naval Forces Central Command HQ. Struck by an Iranian missile on 28 Feb 2026; Bahrain confirmed the HQ was hit; the base was reported to have taken extensive damage. Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain); France 24; Stripes (1 Mar 2026)

markers.name: Mina Salman Port (Bahrain)
markers.note: Struck by an Iranian missile in 2026 (Wikipedia, 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain). Position approximate.

markers.name: Duqm Port (Oman): used by US forces
markers.note: Targeted by Iranian drone and missile strikes in 2026; used by US forces (Wikipedia, 2026 Iranian strikes on Oman). Position approximate.

markers.name: Salalah Port (Oman): used by US forces
markers.note: Targeted by Iranian drone and missile strikes in 2026; used by US forces (Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: Sohar port and industrial zone (Oman)
markers.note: Drone strikes on the port and industrial zone in 2026 (Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: Bukha (Musandam, Oman)
markers.note: Drone strikes on the port in 2026 (Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: Mina al Fahal (near Muscat, Oman)
markers.note: Drone strikes on the port in 2026 (Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: Kuwait International Airport: struck by drones (March 2026)
markers.note: Iranian drones struck the airport and a residential building; two people were wounded (Stripes, 1 Mar 2026).

markers.name: Ras Laffan (Qatar): LNG production halted after Iranian attacks
markers.note: QatarEnergy halted LNG production after Iranian attacks (Al Jazeera, 2 Mar 2026). Position approximate.

markers.name: Kharg Island oil terminal (Iran): not verified in this build
markers.note: Iran's main crude export terminal (public information). Its status in the 2026 war was not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Ceyhan oil terminal (Turkey): not verified in this build
markers.note: Terminal of the Iraq-Turkey crude pipeline (public information). Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: RAF Akrotiri (British Sovereign Base Area, Cyprus): not verified in this build
markers.note: British Sovereign Base Area on Cyprus (the dataset's SBA boundary is drawn). The base's current activity was not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Hmeimim Air Base (Latakia, Syria): Russian air base
markers.note: Syria and Russia signed an MoU on 9 Aug 2026: the base becomes a joint training and capacity-building centre; civilian facilities go to Syria within three months; Russian personnel remain at the new centres (Al Jazeera, Moscow Times). Russia had earlier withdrawn most long-range air-defence systems.
markers.source: Al Jazeera (9 Aug 2026); Moscow Times (9 Aug 2026); Kiprinform (11 Aug 2026)

markers.name: Tartus naval facility (Syria): Russia's Mediterranean repair and supply hub
markers.note: Under the Aug 2026 MoU the facility becomes a joint training centre; Syria takes over the commercial Pier No. 4. Reuters described Tartus as Russia's only Mediterranean repair and replenishment hub. Position approximate (town).
markers.source: Al Jazeera (9 Aug 2026); Wikipedia (Tartus naval base); Reuters (via Kiprinform)

markers.name: Masyaf (Syria): underground missile plant destroyed by Israeli strikes (2024)
markers.note: Underground missile manufacturing facility, reportedly Iran-linked, destroyed by Israeli strikes in 2024 (Wikipedia, 2024 Masyaf raid). Status since then not verified.

markers.name: Bandar Abbas Naval Base (Iran): IRIN facility at the Strait of Hormuz
markers.note: Former headquarters of the IRIN 2nd Naval District (now a support base). Struck on 28 Feb, 2 Mar and 5 Mar 2026; satellite images show the forward base ship IRIS Makran burning at the pier. US unmanned boats struck the raised dock on 12 Jul 2026 (CENTCOM). Position approximate.
markers.source: FDD Long War Journal (Mar 2026); USNI News (2 Mar 2026); CENTCOM (14 Jul 2026, via Interesting Engineering)

markers.name: Bandar Abbas submarine maintenance facility (Iran): Kilo and Ghadir boats
markers.note: Submarine base for the IRIN Southern Fleet. Two Kilo-class boats were in dry dock here at the war's start; the hoist and a Ghadir midget submarine were destroyed on 12 Jul 2026 (Maritime News, citing CENTCOM). FDD reported a Kilo-class boat struck and likely sunk on 28 Feb-5 Mar 2026. Positions approximate.
markers.source: Maritime News (14 Jul 2026); FDD Long War Journal (Mar 2026); USNI News (2 Mar 2026)

markers.name: Jask Naval Base (Iran): IRIN 2nd Naval District headquarters (relocated)
markers.note: The IRIN 2nd Naval District headquarters was moved here from Bandar Abbas (FDD). Position approximate.

markers.name: Konarak Naval Base (Iran): IRIN 3rd Naval District (Gulf of Oman)
markers.note: Headquarters of the IRIN 3rd Naval District, responsible for the Gulf of Oman. Struck at the end of February and early March 2026; an Iranian frigate was reported burning here (USNI; Yahoo News). Position approximate.
markers.source: FDD Long War Journal; USNI News (2 Mar 2026)

markers.name: Chabahar: IRGC Navy Imam Ali Naval Base (deep-water port)
markers.note: Hosts the IRGC Navy's Imam Ali Naval Base; Iran's only port directly on the Indian Ocean (FDD). Struck in 2026; the frigate IRIS Jamaran was reported sunk at the port (Wikipedia). Position approximate.
markers.source: FDD Long War Journal (Mar 2026); Wikipedia (IRIS Jamaran)

markers.name: Bandar Mahshahr: IRGC Navy 3rd Naval District headquarters (northern Gulf)
markers.note: Headquarters of the IRGC Navy's northern Gulf district, near the Iraqi border (FDD). Position approximate.

markers.name: Haifa Naval Base (Israel): main base of the Israeli Navy
markers.note: Main base of the Israeli Navy: Shayetet 7 (submarine flotilla), Shayetet 3 (missile boats), the 914th Patrol Squadron, and the naval shipyard. Position approximate (port area).
markers.source: Wikipedia (Haifa naval base; Shayetet 7); Israel Navy listing

markers.name: Haifa: Shayetet 7 submarine flotilla (6 submarines)
markers.note: Flotilla of about six submarines and 300 personnel, operating Dolphin-class boats. INS Drakon, the sixth submarine and the third Dolphin II, arrived in Haifa in late September 2026 (Algemeiner, 28 Sep 2026). Dakar-class boats are planned from 2033 (Israel Hayom).
markers.source: Wikipedia (Shayetet 7); Algemeiner (28 Sep 2026); Israel Hayom (24 Sep 2026)

markers.name: Dimona (Negev Nuclear Research Center): not confirmed by Israel
markers.note: Israel does not officially confirm the site's purpose (public information). Not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Gölcük Naval Base (Turkey): main base, Fleet Command headquarters
markers.note: Main base of the Turkish Navy on the Sea of Marmara; Fleet Command headquarters; Submarine Group Command; Gölcük Naval Shipyard, which builds the Reis-class and MILDEN-class submarines (Wikipedia, Turkish Naval Forces).
markers.source: Wikipedia (Gölcük Naval Base; Turkish Naval Forces, 2026)

markers.name: Gölcük: Submarine Group Command and shipyard (submarine build)
markers.note: Reis-class (Type 214 derived): S-330 Piri Reis commissioned 24 Aug 2024; S-331 Hızır Reis commissioned 27 Nov 2025; S-332 Murat Reis launched May 2025; three more under construction (Wikipedia). MILDEN-class design is under way at the shipyard (Wikipedia, 2026).
markers.source: Wikipedia (Reis-class submarine; Gölcük Naval Shipyard; Turkish Naval Forces, 2026)

markers.name: Bartın (Turkey): home port of Preveze and Gür-class submarines
markers.note: Home port of the TCG Preveze (S353) and TCG Gür (S357), Type 209/1400 boats built at Gölcük (Turkish Navy ship list). Position approximate (town).
markers.source: Wikipedia (List of active ships of the Turkish Naval Forces)

markers.name: Erdek Naval Base (Turkey): mine warfare group
markers.note: Mine Warfare Group Command is based here (Turkish Navy organisation). Position approximate.

markers.name: ASELSAN (Macunköy, Ankara): electronics, radars, air-defence systems
markers.note: Headquarters and production at Macunköy, Ankara; with Bilkent University it runs Türkiye's first commercial chip factory (GaN). A $6.5bn Steel Dome air-defence contract was signed in November 2025 (Wikipedia). Position approximate.

markers.name: Roketsan (Ankara HQ; new production at Kırıkkale)
markers.note: Turkish missile producer. New facilities at Kırıkkale (warhead facility, missile integration and fuel production), with total investment of about $3bn (Breaking Defense, Apr 2026). Position approximate (Kırıkkale).

markers.name: Baykar (Istanbul HQ; Çorlu test and production area)
markers.note: Drone maker headquartered in Istanbul. KIZILELMA unmanned fighter completed firing tests from its internal bay at Çorlu (Baykar, 2026). Acquired Piaggio Aerospace in December 2024 (Wikipedia). Position approximate (Çorlu).

markers.name: Turkish Aerospace (TUSAŞ/TAI), Ankara
markers.note: Aircraft and aerospace producer headquartered in Ankara (Wikipedia, list of Turkish defence companies). Position approximate.
markers.source: Wikipedia (List of defence companies of Turkey)

markers.name: Natanz (Iran): uranium enrichment complex (FEP and PFEP)
markers.note: Struck by Israel on 13 June 2025 and by the US on 21-22 June 2025 (Operation Midnight Hammer). IAEA reported that the above-ground pilot enrichment plant was destroyed and that power loss may have caused underground damage (ANS, 2026).
markers.source: ANS / Nuclear Newswire (2026); IAEA via Wikipedia; Armscontrol.org (25 Jun 2025)

markers.name: Fordow (Iran): deep underground enrichment plant
markers.note: Struck by the US on 22 June 2025 with bunker-buster weapons (CRS). The IAEA reported no visible damage there on 16 June 2025, before the US strikes; the extent of damage is disputed in the sources.

markers.name: Isfahan Nuclear Technology Center (Iran)
markers.note: IAEA confirmed damage to the chemical laboratory, the uranium conversion plant, the Tehran reactor-fuel plant and the metal-processing facility after the 13 June 2025 Israeli strikes (IAEA via GlobalSecurity). Position approximate.

markers.name: Khondab (Arak) heavy-water reactor (Iran)
markers.note: Struck by Israel on 19 June 2025 (CNN and Al Jazeera key-events lists). The IAEA-cited Armscontrol review says the heavy-water production plant did not appear damaged. Position approximate.

markers.name: Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant (Iran): the country's only operating power reactor
markers.note: Unit 1 is a 915 MWe VVER-1000. The IAEA reported a structure about 350 m from the reactor hit and destroyed on 18 March 2026, and a projectile striking close to the premises on 4 April 2026 (the fourth such incident in recent weeks). Position approximate.
markers.source: ANS / Nuclear Newswire (6 Apr 2026, citing the IAEA)

markers.name: Barakah Nuclear Power Plant (UAE): not verified in this build
markers.note: Four-unit nuclear power plant (public information). Its status in the 2026 war was not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant (Turkey): not verified in this build
markers.note: Under construction on the Mediterranean coast (public information). Its status was not verified in this build.
markers.source: public information (not verified in this build)

markers.name: HESA, Shahin Shahr (Isfahan Province): Ababil and Shahed drones
markers.note: State-owned drone producer (Ababil and Shahed series). Satellite imagery shows at least nine impact points and five damaged buildings from strikes on 1-2 March 2026 (Critical Threats). A Quwa analysis estimates Iranian Shahed output above 200 units a month (an estimate, not verified).

markers.name: Shiraz Electronics Industries (Iran): struck June 2025
markers.note: Struck on 15 June 2025 (JINSA's list of strikes, citing Israeli and US statements). Position approximate.

markers.name: Munitions factory, Isfahan (Iran): drones and ballistic missiles
markers.note: Struck on 15 June 2025; producing drones and ballistic missiles (JINSA). Position approximate.

markers.name: Khojir Missile Production Complex (Hajarabad, Tehran Province)
markers.note: Solid- and liquid-fuel ballistic missile production; struck on 18 June 2025 (JINSA). Position approximate.

markers.name: ODIR (Organization of Defensive Innovation and Research): Tehran HQ, sites in Isfahan, Shiraz, Zahedan, Ahvaz
markers.note: Government research organisation under the Ministry of Defence (Wikipedia). Its headquarters are placed at Tehran; the other sites are not plotted.
markers.source: Wikipedia (Organization of Defensive Innovation and Research)

markers.name: Bid Ganeh ballistic missile facility (Tehran Province)
markers.note: Struck on 2 March 2026; the site likely stored medium-range ballistic missiles (Critical Threats). Position approximate.

markers.name: Kashan Missile Base (Aran va Bidgol, near the 840th Missile Group)
markers.note: Struck on 2 March 2026 (Critical Threats, citing the Martin Center's satellite imagery). Position approximate.

markers.name: Esfahan South Missile Base
markers.note: Struck on 3 March 2026, the third such strike since the conflict began (Critical Threats). Position approximate.

markers.name: Dezful Missile Base (Khuzestan)
markers.note: Airstrikes destroyed at least seven launchers or buildings on or around 4 March 2026 (Critical Threats). Position approximate.

markers.name: Amand missile base (north of Tabriz)
markers.note: Reported to store Ghadr medium-range missiles; struck on 14 and 17 June 2025 (JINSA). Position approximate.

markers.name: Strait of Hormuz: blocked to most shipping since 28 Feb 2026
markers.note: Iran has largely blocked the strait since 28 Feb 2026. The US imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports from 13 Apr 2026; Operation Project Freedom escorted ships from 4-6 May; the ceasefire deal collapsed on 8 July 2026. WTO data show crude shipments down 95% and LNG down 99% (House of Commons Library).
markers.source: House of Commons Library (2026); Wikipedia (2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis; Operation Project Freedom)

markers.name: Bab el-Mandeb: Houthi threats and attacks
markers.note: The Houthis resumed attacks on Israel on 28 March 2026 and threatened the strait (Wikipedia). Israel struck Houthi targets in Yemen from May to October 2025 (Wikipedia).
markers.source: Wikipedia (2026 Houthi strikes on Israel; 2025 Israeli attacks in Yemen)

markers.name: Suez Canal (Ismailia area)
markers.note: Canal linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea (public information).

markers.name: Bosporus (Istanbul straits)
markers.note: Strait linking the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara (public information).

markers.name: Dardanelles (Çanakkale Strait)
markers.note: Strait linking the Aegean and the Sea of Marmara (public information).

markers.name: Tiran Strait (Gulf of Aqaba)
markers.note: Strait at the entrance to the Gulf of Aqaba (public information).

markers.name: Iran: nationwide war since 28 Feb 2026
markers.note: US and Israeli strikes began on 28 Feb 2026 (Operation Epic Fury, US; Roaring Lion, Israel). Ali Khamenei was killed in the first strikes. Iran retaliated against Israel, US bases and Gulf states. A conditional ceasefire on 7 April 2026 was followed by a June MoU that collapsed; fighting resumed on 8 July; the US and Iran were trading limited strikes in September 2026 (CRS R48887; Wikipedia).
markers.source: CRS (R48887, Sep 2026); House of Commons Library (2026); Wikipedia (2026 Iran war)

markers.name: Gulf host states: Iranian missile and drone strikes on US bases and ports (2026)
markers.note: Iranian strikes hit US bases and host infrastructure in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Oman in 2026. The Pentagon's inspector general reports that hundreds of buildings were damaged across US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman and Jordan (CSMonitor, 29 Sep 2026). A GCC statement in June 2026 called for free passage through Hormuz (House of Commons Library).
markers.source: CSMonitor (29 Sep 2026); Wikipedia (2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain, Qatar, Oman); Commons Library (2026)

markers.name: Iraq: strikes on bases hosting US forces (2026)
markers.note: Strikes attributed to Iran or Iran-backed groups hit bases housing US forces during the 2026 war (CRS R48887). A pro-Iranian group, Jaysh al-Ghadab, attacked US positions in Bahrain with drones (Wikipedia). Location is the capital, for orientation only.
markers.source: CRS (R48887); Wikipedia (2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain)

markers.name: Israel: Iranian missile and drone strikes (2025 and 2026)
markers.note: Israel was targeted by Iranian forces in 2025 and 2026; the CRS counts 20 Israeli civilians killed in Iranian attacks before the 7 April 2026 ceasefire. Location is Tel Aviv, for orientation only.

markers.name: Southern Lebanon: Israel-Hezbollah fighting; ceasefires of April and June 2026
markers.note: Israel and Lebanon agreed a ceasefire effective 16 April 2026; Israel and Hezbollah agreed a truce on 1 June 2026; a conditional Israel-Lebanon ceasefire was announced on 4 June 2026. Fighting continued in the south, and Israel expanded its occupation of Lebanese territory (AP, 2 Jun 2026). Figures: 3,980 killed in the 2026 war (Wikipedia; figures contested).
markers.source: Al Jazeera (4 Jun 2026); AP (2 Jun 2026); Wikipedia (Hezbollah-Israel conflict)

markers.name: Gaza: ceasefire since 10 Oct 2025; Israel controls more than 63% of the Strip
markers.note: A ceasefire under the US-backed plan has been in place since 10 Oct 2025. Israel has expanded the area inside the 'Yellow Line' and holds more than 63% of Gaza, per the Gaza Health Ministry and government media office, and continues strikes. More than 1,478 Palestinians were reported killed since the ceasefire (AAWSAT, 10 Oct 2026). Hamas's civil administration resigned on 6 July 2026.

markers.name: Yemen: Houthi attacks on Israel and the Red Sea (2026)
markers.note: The Houthis resumed missile attacks on Israel on 28 March 2026. Israeli strikes in Yemen took place from May to October 2025. The Yemeni civil war has escalated (Wikipedia). Location is Sanaa, for orientation only.
markers.source: Wikipedia (2026 Houthi strikes on Israel; 2026 Iran war status)

markers.name: Syria: transition; Russian bases renegotiated (2026)
markers.note: Russia-Syria MoU of 9 Aug 2026 on the Russian bases (see Hmeimim and Tartus). Other security events in Syria in 2026 were not verified in this build beyond the Masyaf strike of 2024.
markers.source: Al Jazeera (9 Aug 2026); Wikipedia (Tartus naval base)
